hazard: Lack of public access to adrenaline auto-injectors

reports.title: Nasar Ahmed: Prevention of future deaths report

promises.quote: I am hopeful that work underway to change the law to allow schools to hold spare auto-injectors without a named individual prescription, for use as emergency back- up to treat anaphylaxis in children registered by the school as being in receipt of a medical prescription for an auto-injector, will tackle some of the challenges which staff faced in this sad case, and which were set out in your determination.
promises.summary: Schools can hold spare auto-injectors without named prescription starting 1 Oct 2017

promises.quote: Implementation of the Asthma Friendly Schools Project
promises.summary: Implement Asthma Friendly Schools Project to improve asthma management in schools

concerns.quote: generic adrenaline auto-injectors should be available, in much the same way as defibrillators, in public spaces
concerns.hazard: lack of public access to adrenaline auto-injectors

concerns.quote: if a person has an adrenaline auto-injector and: - has any respiratory compromise, or - there is a loss of consciousness, or - if there is doubt, then the correct and potentially lifesaving course of action, regardless of the particular constellation of signs and symptoms, is to use the EpiPen and to use it immediately
concerns.hazard: delayed or omitted adrenaline administration in anaphylaxis

concerns.quote: The asthma pump in Nasar's medication box at school was an Accuhaler, which I heard from his respiratory consultant is inappropriate for an emergency situation such as this, and would not have assisted him.

The school nurse had updated Nasar's care plan by using the allergy action plan (mild-moderate with asthma) instead of the correct one used the year before, the allergy action plan (severe with asthma)
concerns.hazard: inaccurate care plan leading to inadequate emergency instructions

concerns.quote: Not everyone involved in trying to help Nasar was first aid trained, most notably not the learning assistant who was supervising the IER. She said that she would not have thought of looking for and retrieving his care plan
concerns.hazard: lack of trained staff to access emergency care plans

concerns.quote: the school nurse (employed by Compass Wellbeing) conducted a review of Nasar's medication in May 2016, he did not have the medication stored in school in front of him at the time, but relied on its description by a school receptionist
concerns.hazard: inadequate medication verification by non-clinical staff

promises.quote: The EWG AAIs made a number of other recommendations including the reinforcement of critical safety measures to patients on the use and management of AAIs.
promises.summary: Reinforce critical safety measures for AAI use and management

promises.quote: the AAI EWG recommended in principle that AAIs should be made available in public locations for use to treat anaphylaxis in unforeseen, critical circumstances, provided suitable safeguards can be implemented to ensure effective and safe use of the AAIs.
promises.summary: Make AAI devices available in public locations like food retail outlets.

concerns.hazard: lack of timely reporting and registration of food allergy fatalities

concerns.quote: Availability of emergency Adrenaline Auto-injector devices (AAIs) in the Retail food sector
concerns.hazard: absence of emergency adrenaline auto-injectors in food businesses
